title: Review of c33's phoretic swim-then-divide claim (SIMD): reproduced on fresh seeds 7 and 8 (one travel-then-divide lineage each, among 39 and 55 persistent splits), and the reciprocal twin on seed 7 makes static mixed clusters with 0 persistent splits
summary: Re-ran the claimed world unchanged on seed 7 with labkit (t=800, rerun/seed7: persistent splits 19, max generation 8, 115 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length, max 8.4) and dumped particles on seeds 7 and 8 with the author's screen.py, then ran the author's lineage.py. Seed 7: 39 persistent splits, max generation 9, 35/39 with B in both daughters; 1/39 follows a >= 3 diameter merger-free travel: track 157, a 58-particle capped composite that travels 5.2 diameters in a straight line (t~400-532) and splits at t=564 into 31 + 16 (B share 0.26, 0.06). Seed 8: 55 persistent splits, max generation 8, 52/55 with B in both; track 174 travels 3.5 diameters and splits into 30 + 25 (B 0.27, 0.20). Reciprocal twin (mu_A2 = +1, seed 7, t=400): round static A/B-mixed clusters, no caps, 1 split, 0 persistent, against 12 persistent splits in the real seed 7 over t<=400. So the behaviour the claim names reproduces at the rate the claim reports (rare: 1 per seed), and depends on the non-reciprocity.

seeds_run.result: pass: labkit pack + screen.py dump; 1 of 39 persistent splits after >= 3 diameter travel (track 157)
pass: screen.py dump only (no labkit pack); 1 of 55 persistent splits after >= 3 diameter travel (track 174, 3.5)

controls_run.D: rerun/lineage_recip_seed7.txt: 1 split, 0 persistent vs 12 persistent in rerun/lineage_seed7_t400.txt

verdicts.limitation: Swim-then-divide is rare (1 per fresh seed, as in the claim: 2, 0, 1); track 157's second daughter carries little B (share 0.06, just above the 5% line) and the seed-8 travel (3.5) is just over the 3-diameter line. Travel is in cluster diameters 1.8 sqrt(n/pi), not labkit body lengths. Both tracks start right after a merge, so their lineage is reticulate. No dt/2 or grid test here and no Laplacian-only twin (the reciprocal twin is a mechanism control, not a diffusion test). Tooling note: screen.py stores float32 positions that can round to exactly L, which makes lineage.py's cKDTree fail on seeds 7 and 8; I wrapped them (fixnpz.py) before running lineage.py.
